input: Write a due diligence memo on Deel

team.claim: Co-founder Alex Bouaziz is CEO; co-founder Shuo Wang is Chief Revenue Officer (deel.com leadership page, © 2026).

Current executives per Deel's leadership page: Joe Kauffman (President & CFO), Dan Westgarth (COO), Philippe Bouaziz (Executive Chairman & Chief Strategy Officer), Yaron Lavi (CTO), Harish Sharma (Chief Risk Officer), DeAnn Work (Global Corporate General Counsel), Anthony Rodriguez (Chief Compliance Officer).

Joe Kauffman joined as President & CFO (Nov 2025) after a decade at Credit Karma, where he served as CFO, President and CEO, scaling it from $100M+ to $2.3B; founding CFO Philippe Bouaziz (the CEO's father) moved to Executive Chairman & Chief Strategy Officer (company claim).
Recent leadership appointments named by Deel: Harish Sharma as Chief Risk Officer, Anthony Luis Rodriguez as Chief Compliance Officer, DeAnn Work as General Counsel (company claim).
Shuo Wang previously co-founded air-purifier startup Aeris, sold to iRobot in 2021 for $72M; Alex Bouaziz is French and Israeli, MIT attendee, largely based in Tel Aviv (Business Insider, 2023).

Multiple Bouaziz family members in senior roles (2023): father Philippe as CFO/board member, sister Chloe in operations, other relatives in finance and customer success; Philippe was also Deel's founding investor and founder of software firm Prodware.
Notable departure: Elisabeth Diana, head of communications (ex-Instagram/Facebook), resigned April 2025 amid the Rippling spying lawsuit; she had joined in November 2021.
Departure: Zack Shooter (5-year veteran) posted "December 1st was my final day at Deel" (personal LinkedIn post, ~Dec 2025).
Fortune (Nov 2025): ~80% of Deel's leadership team is the same as at $0 ARR (company claim via Fortune).
Board members (aggregator data, GetLatka): Lucas Swisher, Greg Lazarus, Ali Rowghani, Philippe Bouaziz, Yasmin Razavi; investor listed: Anish Acharya.

output.company: Deel (Deel Inc. — deel.com, global HR/payroll platform)

funding.claim: Series E: $300M raised Oct 16, 2025, led by new investor Ribbit Capital alongside existing backers Andreessen Horowitz and Coatue Management, at a $17.3B valuation (Reuters).

Crunchbase: total raised nearly $1.3B since 2019; funds earmarked for acquisitions, expansion to 100+ countries by 2029, and AI offerings; General Catalyst and Green Bay Ventures also participated in the Series E.
Earlier in 2025: ~$300M secondary purchase by General Catalyst and Abu Dhabi's Mubadala at a $12.6B valuation (Reuters).

Prior rounds (aggregator data, GetLatka): Mar/Apr 2019 $150K + $3.9M; Series A May 2020 $14M; Series B Sep 2020 $30M; Series C Apr 2021 $156M ($1B valuation); Series D Oct 2021 $425M ($5B); Series D May 2022 $50M ($12B).

Sacra (aggregator): Series C Apr 2021 $156M led by YC Continuity at $1.25B; Series D Oct 2021 $425M led by Coatue at $5.5B; ~$1.6B total raised; investors include Andreessen Horowitz, Spark Capital, Coatue, Ribbit, General Catalyst, Mubadala.
Company claim (Nov 2025 blog): Deel has secured over $1 billion in funding, with a valuation now exceeding $17.3 billion.

Aggregator data (UseHarvest, as of Nov 9, 2026): total raised $1,259,350,000 across 9 rounds, 32 investors; Series E $300M at $17.3B post-money (aggregator figures conflict with GetLatka's $979.1M/8 rounds).

output.verdict: Deel looks operationally strong: ~$1.5B ARR (H1 2026, company claim), three-plus years of claimed profitability, a $17.3B Series E valuation (Oct 2025), 40,000+ customers and 15 acquisitions — but nearly every financial number is self-reported and unaudited. The decisive red flag is the Rippling corporate-espionage litigation (RICO/DTSA claims largely surviving dismissal in Feb 2026) plus a reported DOJ criminal probe that was still demanding case documents as of November 2026, alongside 2023 lawmaker scrutiny of contractor classification. Closer look needed: the DOJ probe's scope and any charges, the COO-linked payment allegations in court records, actual churn/margin quality behind claimed ARR, and IPO readiness given no S-1 filing as of Nov 9, 2026.

business.claim: Deel is a global HR and payroll platform letting companies hire employees and contractors in 150+ countries without local entities, combining payroll, HR, IT, compliance and benefits (company claim).

Product suite spans EOR, Contractor of Record, PEO, Global and US Payroll, Payroll Engine, HRIS, ATS, immigration, background checks, employee equity, Deel IT, Deel Benefits, Deel Mobility, Deel Embedded and AI products (company claim).

Deel says it owns 250+ legal entities, holds financial licenses in the US, Canada, UK and EU, runs a payroll engine live in 55+ countries and targets real-time native payroll in 100+ countries by 2029 (company claim).
Founded 2019, San Francisco-based, fully remote with employees in over 100 countries.

Business model: SaaS subscription — est. $49/month per active contractor and $599/month per EOR employee, plus payroll, performance-management and IT modules; 25–30% of revenue from fintech services moving over $2B monthly (Sacra estimates, aggregator data).
Customer base spans financial services, healthcare, manufacturing, logistics, gaming, fintech, crypto, AI, BPO, oil & gas, airlines and retail across 150+ countries (company claim, podcast).

traction.claim: "Trusted by 40,000+ companies from startups to enterprise" (company claim on deel.com, as of 2026-11-09).
Reuters: Deel had 6,500 employees and more than 35,000 customers including ElevenLabs, Nike, Klarna and Shopify, competing with Rippling, Omnipresent and ADP.
Processes $22B in payroll annually, 35,000+ customers, 1.5M+ workers on platform, 150+ countries (company claim).
More than 40,000 global customers (company claim, Aug 2026 press); Korean customers named: Toss, Musinsa, LG AI Research.
Named customers include Shopify, Coinbase, Lockheed Martin, ElevenLabs, Lucid, Zillow, On, Puma, Reddit, Klarna, OpenAI, Jelly Belly, NuBank, Instacart (company claim).
Clarity, an AI cybersecurity company (identity verification, deepfake detection, fraud prevention), acquired Aug 2026 — Deel's 15th acquisition; terms not disclosed (company claim).

Acquired Safeguard Global's payroll division in March 2025 for an undisclosed amount; Reuters separately reported the ~$15M acquisition of London-based competitor Omnipresent; Deel earmarked up to $500M for 2025 acquisitions.

2026 partnerships per press roundup: Penfold (UK embedded pensions, Nov 5, 2026), Stripe stablecoin wallet for contractors (Jun 2026), Microsoft Marketplace availability (Jul 2026), stablecoin payouts via Solana (May 2026).
Multiyear Golden State Warriors partnership (Oct 2026) covering Warriors, Valkyries, Santa Cruz Warriors and Chase Center; no contract value disclosed (company announcement via IPO-tracker).
G2 rating 4.7/5 based on 16,139 reviews and 90+ NPS for enterprise customers shown on Deel's own site; Forrester TEI study cited (60% less payroll-processing time, 67% ROI) (company claim).

red_flags.claim: Reported DOJ criminal investigation with grand jury subpoenas (N.D. Cal.) over alleged corporate espionage; if substantiated, executive-directed espionage would represent a governance failure and potential criminal corporate misconduct.
Active RICO/DTSA civil litigation with executives named; court largely denied Deel's motions to dismiss in February 2026; DOJ was still seeking case discovery documents as of November 2026.
Court-record allegations that funds linked to the spy moved through an account held by Deel's COO's wife, plus Deel's admitted "discreet surveillance" of a rival's employee.
US lawmaker letters (2023) seeking investigations into Deel's contractor classification; ~half the workforce on contractor contracts.
Sacra flags regulatory-compliance complexity across 150+ countries (including crypto payroll), margin pressure from competition, and tech-sector hiring concentration as risks (aggregator estimate).
Comms chief departed amid the escalating spying scandal; multiple Bouaziz family members hold senior roles, including the CEO's father as Executive Chairman.

reputation.claim: Glassdoor (aggregator data, as of Nov 9, 2026): 4.3/5 from 2,147 reviews; 84% would recommend to a friend; 89% approve of CEO Alex Bouaziz; compensation & benefits rating down 5% over the last 12 months.

Pattern of critical 2026 reviews (aggregator data): 1★ reviews alleging "toxic petty culture," pressure to leave 5-star Glassdoor reviews within 1–2 weeks of joining, financially incentivized employee influencers, 50–60-hour weeks, and complaints that US payroll "can't consistently pay employees correctly or on time" (unverified employee allegations).

Glassdoor con themes (aggregator data): "CEO and CTO can be very abusive at times"; "Some people almost had to beg for time off"; reviews referencing "Deel redundancy" and job-security outlook in 2026.

Business Insider (2023): 30+ current/former workers described a grow-at-all-costs culture and long hours; workers said they thought they were applying for full-time roles but were hired as long-term contractors; concentration of Bouaziz family members raised staff concerns.

Critical press (Sept 2026): coverage titled "Deel Built 10,000 Agents for Its Own Back Office - Then Added $140M in Revenue Without Hiring. The Self-Reported Math, Examined" questions Deel's self-reported AI-agent operating claims; analysis notes most claimed time savings sit in undescribed workflows.
Counterpoint (company-cited): G2 rating 4.7/5 across 16,139 reviews and Glassdoor Best Places to Work 2025 recognition (company claim / aggregator).

missing_fields: Verified audited financial statements (private company; all revenue/EBITDA figures are company claims or aggregator estimates)
Confirmed data breaches — none found in collected sources
Direct court-docket pulls (PACER/registry) — litigation details sourced from press and law-firm coverage of filings
Confirmed sanctions exposure against Deel — only unproven counter-allegations made by Deel against Rippling in litigation

financial_signals.claim: Reuters (company claim): crossed $1 billion annual revenue run rate in Q1 2025; revenue rose 75% for the twelve months ended April 30; EBITDA margin of 16% for Q1 ended March 31.
Reuters (company claim): crossed $100 million monthly revenue for the first time in September 2025; generates roughly $15–17 million in monthly EBITDA.
Company claim: surpassed $1B ARR earlier in 2025 and three consecutive years of profitability (Oct 2025 funding blog).
Company claim (Aug 4, 2026 press release): surpassed US$1.5 billion ARR in H1 2026 with continued profitable growth.

ARR passed $1.4B in February 2026, up 75% from $800M a year earlier (company claim via GetLatka aggregator; revenue history: $50M Nov 2021, $230M Nov 2022, $400M Jun 2023, $500M Jun 2024, $800M Apr 2025, $1B Oct 2025).
Sacra estimate (aggregator): $1.5B annualized revenue in June 2026, up from $1.3B end of 2025; 62.5% y/y growth; 85% gross margins; EBITDA-positive since September 2022 at ~15% margin (16% in 2025).
Headcount: 6,500 employees as of June 2025 (Reuters); ~7,000 (just over) per company claim in Jan 2026 interview, with COO Dan Westgarth's org at 3,300.
Aggregator data (UseHarvest, Nov 9, 2026): 9,641 employees; latest secondary price $33.06/share (Caplight model), implying ~$14.7B valuation, -15% vs the $38.92 Series E price (aggregator data).
Hiring: running a virtual hiring event to fill 300+ Sales/GTM roles on Jan 14, 2026 (company claim).

Company claim (Sept 2026): 8,000+ AI agents on its internal Akai platform do the work of ~600 full-time employees; added $140M+ ARR in 90 days without increasing headcount; revenue per employee grew from $130K to $215K — press notes none of these figures is independently audited and akai.run claims 10,000+ live agents (discrepancy unreconciled).
IPO status: as of Nov 9, 2026 Deel has not filed publicly for an IPO — no S-1/F-1 on SEC EDGAR; no listing date announced (IPO tracker).

legal_and_regulatory.claim: March 2025: Rippling sued Deel in the U.S. District Court for the Northern District of California, alleging Deel "cultivated a spy to systematically steal its competitor's most sensitive business information and trade secrets" (sales leads, pipeline, prospecting playbook).

June 2025: amended complaint named several Deel executives and alleged Deel directed a "racketeering enterprise" victimizing at least four companies, claiming RICO and Defend Trade Secrets Act violations, including crypto payments to an existing Rippling employee to steal trade secrets.
February 2026: N.D. Cal. found some state-law claims preempted but largely denied motions to dismiss the remainder of Rippling's suit.

Per WSJ, the DOJ has reportedly opened a criminal investigation into Deel over allegations it hired a corporate spy to leak information on Rippling; Deel says it is "not aware of any investigation" and will cooperate with authorities.
The report indicates U.S. Attorney Craig H. Missakian (N.D. Cal.) has issued grand jury subpoenas seeking documents related to the alleged spying operation.
November 2026: DOJ subpoenaed Rippling seeking all documents produced during discovery in the espionage lawsuit against Deel, per court filings — the probe remained active as of Nov 2026.

Court documents in late November 2025 showed bank records indicating Deel transferred funds into an account held by the wife of Deel's COO, which 56 seconds later transferred the same amount to the confessed spy's account (allegation in court records).

Deel admitted it instructed "discreet surveillance" on the manager at the center of the spy case (Irish Times, June 2025); a Rippling employee confessed in an Irish court to being a paid spy for Deel, handing over sales leads, product roadmaps and customer account info.

April 2, 2025: Rippling released a sworn affidavit from employee Keith O'Brien appearing to confirm Deel planted a spy; O'Brien later said that at the urging of Deel executives he made false statements to authorities that Rippling was facilitating Russian payments; Deel denied all legal wrongdoing and called the suit frivolous.

Deel countersued Rippling (Delaware state court) for defamation and alleged Rippling ran its own espionage scheme to copy Deel's products; Deel also claims a Rippling employee leaked documents purporting to show Rippling facilitated payments to sanctioned jurisdictions including Russia (sanctions counter-allegation, unproven).

2023 regulatory attention: Rep. Adam Schiff and other US lawmakers wrote to acting Labor Secretary Julie Su calling for an investigation into Deel's use of independent contractors; California Sen. Stephen Padilla wrote the state labor agency; at least half of Deel's workforce are contractors with misclassification concerns raised by 17 current/former workers.

Deel acknowledged it made a payment of approximately $6,000 to Rippling employee Keith O'Brien; the companies offer conflicting accounts of whether it was part of an effort to extract trade secrets (Calcalist, Aug 2026).
